past_medical_history: HIV positive, on antiretroviral therapy, undetectable viral load

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Good historian.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Tongue midline with mild left-sided fasciculations. No dysarthria. Jaw jerk mildly brisk.
neurological_exam.motor: Left arm: shoulder abduction 4/5, elbow flexion 4/5, hand intrinsic 3+/5, thenar atrophy visible. Right arm: 4+/5 throughout. Bilateral leg: mild hip flexor weakness 4+/5, otherwise 5/5. Visible fasciculations bilateral arms.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 3+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 3+. Knee jerks 3+. Ankle jerks 2+. Hoffman bilateral. Left Babinski positive.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly spastic — note: gait spasticity was attributed to HIV myelopathy previously.
neurological_exam.additional: HIV-positive patient with combined upper and lower motor neuron signs, including limb and tongue fasciculations.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive arm and leg weakness over 10 months in HIV-positive patient on ART
patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. T is a 46-year-old woman living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load presenting with 10-month progressive arm and leg weakness. She was diagnosed with HIV 12 years ago and has been stably treated on bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide for 3 years with consistently undetectable viral load and CD4 count >500 cells/uL.

She first noticed left arm weakness and wasting 10 months ago and was initially referred to HIV neurology given concern for HIV-related complications. However, the pattern of weakness with visible muscle twitching and fasciculations, combined with hyperreflexia and a Babinski sign, is not typical of HIV myelopathy (vacuolar myelopathy) or HIV-associated neuropathy.

Her HIV neurologist considered HIV vacuolar myelopathy, CMV radiculopathy, and lymphoma as possible etiologies. MRI spine was obtained and showed no vacuolar changes, no cord compression, no lymphoma. CD4 count 520 cells/uL argues against opportunistic CNS processes. The fasciculations in the arms and the left tongue, together with combined upper and lower motor neuron signs, prompted further neurological evaluation.

signal_characteristics.T2: No vacuolar change, no signal abnormality

additional_observations: No HIV vacuolar myelopathy pattern (posterior column T2 change typically)
mri.impression: No cord signal change. No cord compression. No mass lesion. No leptomeningeal enhancement. No posterior column T2 signal change

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: CD4/CD8 ratio 0.9 ratio (L), CK 624 U/L (H), JC virus serology Positive (1:64) titer (H).

findings.finding: Left FDI, APB: fibrillations +2, complex fasciculation potentials, large MUPs, reduced recruitment. Right FDI: fasciculations complex, sparse fibrillations. Cervical paraspinals: fibrillations +1.
Right tibialis anterior: fasciculations, mildly large MUPs. Sparse fibrillations.
All sensory studies normal; no distal symmetric sensory loss.
Reduced CMAP amplitudes. Normal conduction velocities. No conduction block.

quantitative_data.pattern: Multi-region motor denervation with paraspinal involvement; sensory NCS normal, no distal symmetric pattern
quantitative_data.regions: Cervical and bulbar active denervation; thoracic and lumbosacral fibrillations

specialized_test.impression: Active denervation (fibrillations +2, positive sharp waves) and chronic reinnervation (large amplitude, polyphasic MUPs, reduced recruitment) in the cervical and bulbar regions; fibrillations +1 in thoracic and lumbosacral regions. Sensory NCS entirely normal. Reduced CMAP amplitudes with preserved conduction velocities; no conduction block. Findings indicate a widespread disorder of anterior horn cells

interactions: Bictegravir (integrase inhibitor): metabolized primarily by CYP3A4. Riluzole is CYP1A2 substrate. Minimal direct DDI. Coadministration is feasible.
Tenofovir alafenamide: renal elimination, no CYP1A2 interaction.
warnings: Monthly LFT monitoring for riluzole. Note: biktarvy components can affect liver enzymes — baseline LFTs and close monitoring critical
Consult HIV pharmacist to confirm no interactions with specific ART regimen
alternatives: AMX0035 — check with HIV specialist for any ART interactions

results.title: ALS in HIV-infected patients
results.finding: Case reports and series describe ALS in people living with HIV. HIV does not cause ALS but can co-occur. Well-controlled HIV with undetectable viral load effectively rules out HIV-driven motor neuron disease. Management is same as HIV-negative ALS patients.

results.title: HIV neurology differential diagnosis — motor weakness
results.finding: HIV motor weakness ddx: vacuolar myelopathy (posterior column MRI changes), HIV-associated neuropathy (sensory predominant), CMV radiculomyelopathy (CD4<100), PML (white matter lesions). ALS with fasciculations, LMN+UMN combined, paraspinal denervation not characteristic of any HIV complication.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. Rhythmic midtemporal theta of drowsiness, a benign normal variant of no clinical significance.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

findings: Trace mitral regurgitation, physiological. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
echo.impression: Structurally near-normal heart with a benign incidental finding.

findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) concurrent with virologically suppressed HIV

differential.key_features: Reported HIV-associated ALS-like syndromes typically with uncontrolled viremia; this patient is suppressed
Predominantly UMN with sensory involvement; sensory NCS here is normal
Tenofovir and integrase inhibitors not classically associated; pattern is motor only
Brain/spine MRI excludes structural cord disease
Neurogenic EMG pattern with fasciculations excludes IBM

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI (with cervical spine sequences) to exclude structural mimics — cervical myelopathy, demyelination, brainstem tumor
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No structural lesion explaining the motor/bulbar findings; corticospinal-tract signal change or non-specific findings may be seen but are not by themselves diagnostic

optimal_actions.action: Perform EMG with nerve conduction studies sampling bulbar plus ≥2 spinal regions to document lower motor neuron involvement (fibrillations, positive sharp waves, complex fasciculation potentials, large-amplitude long-duration polyphasic MUPs with reduced recruitment) and exclude conduction block
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Active denervation and chronic reinnervation in ≥2 body regions with normal sensory NCS and no conduction block — meets Awaji / El Escorial revised criteria

optimal_actions.action: Order a mimic-exclusion lab panel: CK, B12, TSH, HbA1c, HIV, RPR, SPEP, anti-GM1 IgM antibodies, and (in males) androgen receptor CAG repeat for Kennedy disease
optimal_actions.expected_finding: CK often mildly to moderately elevated (2–5× ULN); reversible mimics (B12, TSH, HIV, RPR) negative; anti-GM1 negative; SPEP without high-titer M-spike; CAG repeat normal

optimal_actions.action: Measure respiratory function (FVC, MIP/MEP, SNIP/NIF) at baseline to inform NIV timing and prognostication
optimal_actions.expected_finding: FVC and SNIP/MIP often reduced even in early disease; values guide timing of NIV (FVC <50% predicted or SNIP <40 cmH₂O are conventional thresholds)

optimal_actions.action: Search the medical literature to confirm Awaji and Gold Coast diagnostic thresholds and AAN practice-parameter recommendations relevant to this presentation
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Awaji-Shima 2008 / Gold Coast 2020 diagnostic criteria; AAN 2009 practice parameter on ALS care

tool_parameters.query: ALS diagnostic criteria Awaji Gold Coast AAN practice parameter

optimal_actions.action: Order an ALS-focused genetic panel (C9orf72 repeat expansion, SOD1, TARDBP, FUS, TBK1) — required when family history is positive or onset is young (<50)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: C9orf72 expansion in ~40% of familial cases; SOD1/TARDBP/FUS in additional familial subset; ~10% of apparently sporadic cases also carry a variant

optimal_actions.action: Obtain CSF for neurofilament light chain (NfL) for prognostic stratification when the diagnosis remains uncertain or when prognostic information will change management
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Markedly elevated CSF NfL (typically >5,000 pg/mL) supports a motor-neuron-disease degenerative process and correlates with faster progression

optimal_actions.action: Check interactions before initiating riluzole 50 mg twice daily; review baseline LFTs and CBC and counsel on monitoring
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No major interactions for typical chronic medications; advise alcohol and grapefruit-juice avoidance (CYP1A2 modulators); monthly LFTs for first 3 months

useless_tools.rationale: ALS is a motor-neuron disease without cortical electrical signature; EEG has no diagnostic role and adds cost without benefit.
ECG is unrelated to motor neuron disease and not part of the standard ALS workup absent specific cardiac symptoms or pre-medication QTc checks.
Echocardiography is unrelated to ALS diagnosis; no indication absent comorbid cardiac disease.
Cardiac monitoring has no role in ALS diagnostic workup.
MRI is the standard structural study for ALS workup; head CT adds no diagnostic value and exposes the patient to ionizing radiation.
Amyloid PET has no role in ALS diagnosis (motor-neuron rather than amyloid pathology) and carries a high cost.
DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic integrity; it has no role in ALS, which spares the dopaminergic system.
FDG-PET has no established diagnostic role in ALS and adds substantial cost.

critical_actions: Perform EMG/NCS sampling the bulbar region plus ≥2 spinal regions to document lower-motor-neuron involvement and exclude conduction block.
Obtain brain MRI to exclude structural mimics (cervical myelopathy, demyelinating disease, brainstem tumor).
Order a mimic-exclusion lab panel (CK, B12, TSH, HIV, RPR, SPEP, anti-GM1 IgM, androgen receptor CAG repeat in males).
Measure baseline respiratory function (FVC, MIP/MEP, SNIP) to inform NIV timing.
Apply Awaji-Shima 2008 / Gold Coast 2020 criteria to confirm the diagnosis.
Initiate riluzole 50 mg twice daily after baseline LFTs unless contraindicated; arrange monthly LFT monitoring for the first 3 months.
Refer to a multidisciplinary ALS clinic for SLP, dietetics, respiratory, and social-work input.
contraindicated_actions: Do not commit the patient to cervical spine surgery on the basis of incidental spondylotic changes when EMG findings extend beyond the cervical cord.
Do not start chronic immunosuppression (steroids, IVIG, plasma exchange) for ALS — there is no benefit and treatment delays correct diagnosis.
Do not defer respiratory assessment in a symptomatic patient — even mild FVC reduction warrants close monitoring and NIV planning.
Do not dismiss bulbar or progressive symptoms as functional / psychiatric without a complete neurological workup.
key_reasoning_points: Diagnosis requires evidence of both upper-motor-neuron involvement (hyperreflexia, Babinski, Hoffman, brisk jaw jerk, spasticity) and lower-motor-neuron involvement (atrophy, fasciculations, EMG denervation) with progressive spread, while excluding mimics — Awaji 2008 / Gold Coast 2020.

EMG in bulbar plus ≥2 spinal regions documenting fibrillations, positive sharp waves, complex fasciculation potentials, and large-amplitude long-duration polyphasic MUPs with reduced recruitment satisfies the electrodiagnostic criterion.
Normal sensory NCS and absence of conduction block are pivotal: they exclude common mimics including multifocal motor neuropathy, CIDP, and Kennedy disease.
Mild-to-moderate CK elevation (2–5× ULN) is consistent with ALS and does not itself indicate a primary myopathy.
Cervical spondylotic changes on MRI are common incidental findings in the at-risk age group; bulbar findings or multi-region EMG denervation cannot be attributed to cervical disease.
Baseline FVC, MIP/MEP, and SNIP/NIF inform NIV timing — NIV initiation at FVC <50% predicted or SNIP <40 cmH₂O prolongs survival and improves quality of life.
Markedly elevated CSF neurofilament light chain (>5,000 pg/mL) supports motor neuron degeneration and correlates with progression rate (ENCALS prediction model).

red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests HIV-associated motor neuropathy or ART-related neuromuscular complications
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Virologically suppressed HIV with normal CD4 makes HIV-associated motor neuron syndrome unlikely; EMG/UMN findings are classic ALS

metadata.notes: ALS in well-controlled HIV patient. Systematic exclusion of HIV-related neurological complications required. Normal sensory NCS and combined UMN/LMN pattern confirms ALS.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: HIV introduces ALS-mimic differential (HIV-associated motor neuronopathy) requiring literature support; well-controlled HIV reduces but does not eliminate diagnostic ambiguity
